name: State Association
character: An umbrella organization: steady governance voice in forest green for a state's worth of chapters, one big spring gathering, and a teaching-grant fund.

sections.heading: How the association works
sections.html:
Every chapter holds one seat on the board, and the board meets on the second Wednesday in {{city}} or by video when the roads are bad. Dues are split three ways: half stays with programs, a quarter funds the grants, and a quarter keeps the insurance and the post office box.

The bylaws fit on eleven pages and have survived thirty years of amendments, mostly about the raffle table.

sections.title: Join through your chapter, or as a member at large
sections.body: Dues are twenty-five dollars a year, and membership travels with you if you move across the state.

sections.heading: Starting a chapter
sections.html: A chapter charter takes six members, a name nobody else has used, and a one-page application to the board. New chapters pay no association dues for their first year, and the grants committee visits any chapter that asks for help planning programs.

sections.heading: The gathering, in short
sections.html: Held the third weekend of April in a building with bad carpet and wonderful light. Registration opens in January, fills by the end of February, and the challenge quilts go up before the coffee does. The full schedule lives on the events page.

sections.title: Membership in the association
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: For quilters, for chapters, and for the shops that keep every one of us in backing fabric.

sections.heading: Where the twenty-five dollars goes
sections.html: Half funds programs, a quarter funds the teaching grants, and the rest pays the liability insurance that every chapter borrows for its shows. Open the membership form and choose individual, chapter, or business membership.

items.q: My guild is small. Can we affiliate?
items.a: Yes. Chapter dues scale with size, and a chapter of eight has the same board seat as a chapter of eighty.

items.q: Can I join without a chapter?
items.a: Member at large is a real category, and members at large get first pick of gathering classes because they have no chapter waiting list to negotiate.
January first, pro-rated after June. The membership chair sends two reminders and one polite postcard.

sections.title: About {{guild_name}}
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: Founded when five guilds met at a county fairground and decided the state needed one calendar.

sections.heading: Thirty years of calendars
sections.html:
The founding complaint, preserved in the first minutes, was that five guilds scheduled shows on the same three weekends every year and nobody could attend anybody else's. The association began as a shared calendar and grew the programs the calendar made possible.

It is a not-for-profit run by a board of chapter representatives. The records live in four archival boxes at the historical society, and the traveling trophy for the chapter challenge lives wherever it was last won, which has caused disputes of the friendly kind.
